summary_paragraph: A woman with prior laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, history of gastrojejunal ulcers, cyclic vomiting syndrome, and gastrostomy tube dependence for poor oral tolerance was admitted with two days of left upper quadrant pain localized near the G-tube site and baseline nausea/vomiting without fever, diarrhea, or constipation. Labs were reassuring, and she underwent fluoroscopy-guided interventional radiology exchange/replacement of the gastrostomy tube along the same tract with treatment of local granulation tissue; pain improved and was managed with oral analgesics and a lidocaine patch. Given that the tube was positioned in the gastric pouch (contiguous with the esophagus), the team discussed that feeding through it might not be beneficial for cyclic vomiting-related nutrition support; tube removal was offered but deferred by the patient. She was restarted on home medications including pantoprazole and sucralfate, tolerated oral intake, remained ambulatory and mentally clear, and was discharged home with tube-site care instructions and plans for outpatient follow-up and endoscopy to delineate anatomy and guide longer-term nutrition management.
